# AI Consultation Deadlines Canada

> Every channel through which people in Canada can shape how AI is governed -- federal consultations, calls for briefs, Canada Gazette comment periods, funding calls, standards reviews and e-petitions -- each with a plain-language summary, why it matters for AI safety, and a concrete way to take part.

Built 2026-09-07. 26 items tracked: 13 open, 0 closing within 7 days, 13 retired. Curated by hand Mondays and Thursdays; every record carries a `verified` flag saying whether a person has checked its dates and links against the source page.

Status is derived, not asserted: `new` means opened or first seen within 14 days,
`closing soon` means the stated closing date is within 7 days, `retired` means past that
date or withdrawn. Always confirm a deadline on the official page before submitting.

Content is multilingual (English and French); translated fields are suffixed `_fr` and fall back to English when a translation is not yet written. Data is CC BY 4.0 -- reuse it freely with
attribution to AI Consultation Deadlines Canada. Underlying government content is reproduced under the Open Government Licence - Canada.

## Structured data

- [items.json](https://donjguido.github.io/ai-consultation-deadlines-canada/items.json): every record, full fields. Start here.
- [feed.json](https://donjguido.github.io/ai-consultation-deadlines-canada/feed.json): JSON Feed 1.1, newest first, with a `_monitor` object per item carrying status, deadline and verification.
- [llms-full.txt](https://donjguido.github.io/ai-consultation-deadlines-canada/llms-full.txt): every item as Markdown, the whole corpus in one fetch.
- [feed.xml](https://donjguido.github.io/ai-consultation-deadlines-canada/feed.xml): RSS 2.0, English.
- [feed-fr.xml](https://donjguido.github.io/ai-consultation-deadlines-canada/feed-fr.xml): RSS 2.0, French.
- [digest.md](https://donjguido.github.io/ai-consultation-deadlines-canada/digest.md): this week's digest. [digest-fr.md](https://donjguido.github.io/ai-consultation-deadlines-canada/digest-fr.md) in French.
- [forks.json](https://donjguido.github.io/ai-consultation-deadlines-canada/forks.json): this site and its sister sites for other geographies.

## Live query

An MCP server exposes the same store as tools an agent can call directly -- `list_open`,
`closing_soon`, `list_new`, `search`, `get_item`, `list_topics`, `monitor_status` -- so an
assistant can answer "what is open right now" without fetching and re-parsing this site.
See [docs/MCP.md](https://github.com/donjguido/ai-consultation-deadlines-canada/blob/main/docs/MCP.md).

## Closing within 7 days

- Nothing closing in the next 7 days.

## New in the last 14 days

- [AI Compute Challenge: call for proposals](https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/ised/en/canadian-sovereign-ai-compute-strategy/ai-compute-challenge): Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, no stated deadline. Up to $700M for commercial or consortium proposals to build domestic AI data-centre capacity, with priority to projects that keep sensitive data in Canada. Applications accepted on an ongoing basis.
- [Senate RIDR study on the impact of AI on human rights and economic security](https://sencanada.ca/en/committees/RIDR/): Standing Senate Committee on Human Rights, no stated deadline. Examines AI's effects on human rights and economic security, especially for vulnerable groups and the right to work. Spring 2026 hearings covered algorithmic discrimination, job displacement and children.
- [INDU study: Opportunities, Risks, and Regulation of AI in Canada's Strategic Industries](https://www.ourcommons.ca/committees/en/INDU/StudyActivity?studyActivityId=13310104): House of Commons Standing Committee on Industry and Technology, no stated deadline. House industry committee study on AI risks and regulation across strategic sectors. 46 witnesses and 23 briefs so far; no report yet. Last meeting 16 June 2026.
- [Citizenship Regulations amendments: mandatory biometrics for citizenship applicants](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/acts-regulations/forward-regulatory-plan/list/amending-citizenship-regulations-biometric-information.html): Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, no stated deadline. Proposed rule requiring fingerprints and a facial image from all citizenship applicants. IRCC's forward regulatory plan targets Canada Gazette Part I pre-publication in 2026 with a roughly 30-day comment period.

## All open items

- [Have your say on advancing AI transparency in Canada](https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/ised/en/have-your-say-advancing-ai-transparency-canada): Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, closes 2026-09-23. Two-month consultation under the AI for All strategy on five transparency mechanisms: detecting AI-generated content, disclosing when people interact with AI, standardized information about AI systems, tracking serious AI incidents, and tracking the activities of AI agents.
- [CAN/DGSI 138 Patient-Visible and Accountable AI in Clinical Decision Support: public review](https://dgc-cgn.org/product/patient-visible-and-accountable-ai-in-clinical-decision-support/): Digital Governance Standards Institute, closes 2026-10-05. 60-day public review of a proposed National Standard of Canada setting governance, transparency, human-oversight and lifecycle-monitoring requirements for AI clinical decision support.
- [AI Compute Challenge: call for proposals](https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/ised/en/canadian-sovereign-ai-compute-strategy/ai-compute-challenge): Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, no stated deadline. Up to $700M for commercial or consortium proposals to build domestic AI data-centre capacity, with priority to projects that keep sensitive data in Canada. Applications accepted on an ongoing basis.
- [Senate SOCI study on the impact of artificial intelligence in Canada](https://sencanada.ca/en/committees/SOCI/45-1): Standing Senate Committee on Social Affairs, Science and Technology, no stated deadline. Order of reference to examine data governance and sovereignty; ethics, privacy and safety; and the risks, benefits and social impact of AI. An interim report on a human-centred approach has been published; the final report is due by 31 December 2026.
- [Senate RIDR study on the impact of AI on human rights and economic security](https://sencanada.ca/en/committees/RIDR/): Standing Senate Committee on Human Rights, no stated deadline. Examines AI's effects on human rights and economic security, especially for vulnerable groups and the right to work. Spring 2026 hearings covered algorithmic discrimination, job displacement and children.
- [Senate TRCM study on AI in the information and communication technology sector](https://sencanada.ca/en/committees/trcm/): Standing Senate Committee on Transport and Communications, no stated deadline. Covers AI in content creation and distribution, copyright and IP implications, and AI-generated disinformation and deepfakes. Written submissions were requested by 1 May 2026 but briefs are still accepted; the report is due by 31 December 2027.
- [INDU study: Opportunities, Risks, and Regulation of AI in Canada's Strategic Industries](https://www.ourcommons.ca/committees/en/INDU/StudyActivity?studyActivityId=13310104): House of Commons Standing Committee on Industry and Technology, no stated deadline. House industry committee study on AI risks and regulation across strategic sectors. 46 witnesses and 23 briefs so far; no report yet. Last meeting 16 June 2026.
- [ETHI study: Challenges Posed by Artificial Intelligence and its Regulation](https://www.ourcommons.ca/committees/en/ethics/StudyActivity?studyActivityId=13255402): House of Commons Standing Committee on Access to Information, Privacy and Ethics, no stated deadline. Seven meetings from November 2025 to February 2026, including the Privacy Commissioner. 20 witnesses and 10 briefs; no report tabled and no meeting since 26 February 2026.
- [SRSR study: Artificial Intelligence in innovation and scientific research](https://www.ourcommons.ca/committees/en/SRSR/StudyActivity?studyActivityId=13232926): House of Commons Standing Committee on Science and Research, no stated deadline. Study on AI research advances, research-institution needs, the federal role in a responsible AI research ecosystem, and protection of Canadian discoveries. 19 briefs; last meeting 12 February 2026.
- [Bill C-34, Safe Social Media Act: committee study of AI chatbot duties](https://www.parl.ca/legisinfo/en/bill/45-1/c-34): Canadian Heritage / House of Commons, no stated deadline. Introduced 10 June 2026, the bill would impose safety and disclosure duties on social media and AI chatbot services, especially toward children, enforced by a new Digital Safety Commission. Committee study and a briefs window are expected in the fall sitting.
- [Bill C-36, Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act: committee study](https://www.parl.ca/legisinfo/en/bill/45-1/c-36): Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada / House of Commons, no stated deadline. Introduced 15 June 2026 to replace PIPEDA. Secondary sources say it omits AI but includes obligations for automated decision-making in some circumstances.
- [Citizenship Regulations amendments: mandatory biometrics for citizenship applicants](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/acts-regulations/forward-regulatory-plan/list/amending-citizenship-regulations-biometric-information.html): Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, no stated deadline. Proposed rule requiring fingerprints and a facial image from all citizenship applicants. IRCC's forward regulatory plan targets Canada Gazette Part I pre-publication in 2026 with a roughly 30-day comment period.
- [Notice of intent: Guidance for AI Regulatory Measures, Directives and Policies (CSA Group)](https://scc-ccn.ca/standards/notices-of-intent/csa-group/guidance-ai-regulatory-measures-directives-and-policies): Standards Council of Canada / CSA Group, no stated deadline. Planned CSA standard guiding Canadian regulators and ministries on building coherent, ethical and transparent AI policies aligned with ISO/IEC 42001 and 23894. Public review date not yet published.
